subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the public contract be global, per-agent, hostname-scoped, or folded into broader egress policy?
rationale: This changes an SSRF boundary and public config contract; the primitive exists in lower-level code, but policy shape, authorization, hard-deny behavior, and upgrade semantics require maintainer/security intent before implementation.

options.title: Approve a dangerous scoped policy
options.body: Land a narrowly documented `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design that allows private-network access only with explicit operator intent plus audit, redirect, cache, and metadata safeguards.

options.title: Keep only narrow fake-IP support
options.body: Leave current main as-is and document that arbitrary private-network `web_fetch` remains intentionally unsupported for now.

options.title: Route through broader egress policy
options.body: Fold this into the broader web-tool egress firewall work so private-network access, domain allowlists, and per-agent authorization are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve a dangerous scoped policy
recommendation.body: Land a narrowly documented `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design that allows private-network access only with explicit operator intent plus audit, redirect, cache, and metadata safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest direct issue-thread and code-history connection to the SSRF and guarded-fetch boundary decision.
